description: The arena-sim mirror match (one extractor-barracks pair per half) as a whole battle on a generated neutral zone.
Six tier 3 barracks lines (rush) against walls, three turrets, two armories, an overclocker and two barracks (fortify and ramp).
Four tier 3 barracks lines against a bare Core: over quickly.
Two Cores in wall rings and no producers: Overload destroys both Cores on the same tick; equal overkill, no building damage and no kills, so the attacker (side 0) wins.

Two players per side, Cores only. Side 1 player 0 has a Core of 20 health that Overload destroys at tick 2000; the battle goes on and ends at tick 3100, when the three other Cores fall together. Side 0 overkill is 25 + 25, side 1 only 25 (the Core that fell earlier adds nothing): the defender wins on the overkill rung.
Four players per side, every Core in a wall ring and no producers: Overload destroys all eight Cores at tick 3100 and the attacker (side 0) wins the tie.
Two players per side. Side 1 loses a Core to Overload at the first beat; the other three have 30000 health and survive to the 12000-tick limit: side 0 has more Cores standing and wins (time_limit).
As the Cores-standing vector but side 0 loses a Core: the defender (side 1) wins on Cores standing.
Two players per side, all four Cores survive to the limit. Side 0 keeps 3735 + 3735 of 60000 Core health, side 1 3735 + 1735: side 0 wins on the share of total Core health (time_limit).
Two players per side. All four Cores fall at tick 3100. Side 0 overkill is 0 + 3, side 1 0 + 0: the lower overkill wins (tiebreak_overkill), so the defender wins.

Equal overkill, decided by damage to enemy buildings before kills: side 1 sends one soldier (a scheduled wave) at a Core in a wall ring with a tier 1 turret in front that needs no supply (free power). The soldier hits the turret for 18 damage before it dies, so side 1 dealt more damage to buildings although side 0 killed more units; both Cores fall to Overload decay on the same tick with the same overkill and side 1 wins.

Equal overkill and no damage to buildings on either side, decided by units killed: side 0 sends three soldiers (a scheduled wave) at a Core guarded by five tier 3 turrets that need no supply (free power); the turrets kill all three before they reach anything. Both Cores fall to Overload decay on the same tick with the same overkill and side 1, with three kills, wins.
Two bare Cores and nothing else: equal overkill, no damage to buildings, no kills, so the attacker (side 0) wins the final rung when Overload decay destroys both Cores on the same tick.

Both Cores have 30000 health and survive Overload decay to the 12000-tick limit. Side 1 loses a few more Core health points (a soldier of side 0 reaches its Core before a tier 2 turret kills it (the turret stands at x = 15, a little farther from the Core than before the units became circles, so that the soldier gets its two blows in)) than side 0 loses to a soldier of side 1 that only hits a walled turret: side 0 wins on the Core health fraction (time_limit) although side 1 has dealt more building damage.
The mirror of battle.time-limit-fraction-side0 with the sides swapped: side 1 wins on the Core health fraction at the time limit although side 0 has dealt more building damage.

Both Cores have 30000 health and lose only to decay, so the Core health fractions are equal at the 12000-tick limit. A soldier of side 1 hits a walled turret of side 0 (building damage 18) and dies; side 0's turret has the kill. Side 1 wins on building damage (the kills rung would give side 0).
Equal Core health fractions at the time limit and no building damage on either side: free-power turrets of side 1 kill a wave of side 0 and side 1 wins on kills (the attacker rung would give side 0).
Two bare Cores of 30000 health: everything is equal at the time limit and side 0, the attacker, wins.
One plot against two plots is refused before anything else.

error.message: Both sides must have the same party size: the boards are 24 and 48 cells wide.

description: A scheduled wave of 1200 soldiers (side 1) is larger than the front row holds: the units that find no room wait in the entering queue in order and come in as the row clears; none is dropped. The party Core is strong enough that the battle outlasts the queue.
